terra.problem: The text does not say Jonah had just gone overboard or that the fish was already on its way. Those details add timing and movement.
The explanation gives away the later appointment of the plant in an unfinished story.
It gives away the later appointment of the east wind and says “Wrong weather, wrong chapter” about the baker’s answer.
The explanation is generic and flat. “Three days is already plenty” is a mild observation where the situation could carry a stronger laugh.
It states a Bible fact about other stories without a reference.
The text does not establish where the king of Nineveh is relative to the sea. It also does not establish that Jonah has never been to Nineveh before.
Jonah says he will look toward the temple. The explanation turns that into an action he is performing.
Jonah says he will look toward the temple; the text does not say his eyes actually go there or contrast their direction with a shoreline.
Saying Jonah is looking treats his stated intention to look toward the temple as an action the text reports.
The explanation is generic and mostly repeats that remembered is the word in the text, without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The explanation is flat and formulaic, repeating the answer with little personality.
